title: Rate-Induced Tipping in a Non-Uniformly Moving Habitat and Determination of the Critical Rate
summary: A habitat that is moving due to environmental change may result in tipping to extinction if the rate at which it moves is too great. We use a scalar reaction-diffusion equation with a non-autonomous reaction term, representing a spatially localized habitat moving from one asymptotic location to another, as a context for studying this phenomenon. The movement is characterized by displacement $d$ and rate parameter $r$.
